children.text: UPER Education & Tech, in collaboration with Tarumanagara Xinya College, successfully co-hosted the Tarumanagara Xinya College Career Forum 2026, themed
"Unlocking Your Career Potential: Success Strategies for Mandarin Language Graduates in the Global Industry."

The forum brought together university students to explore the evolving career landscape for Mandarin graduates and gain a deeper understanding of the competencies required in today's international workplace.

As part of the collaboration, UPER Education & Tech also participated in the university's Job Fair, where the team introduced career opportunities at UPER, particularly for Mandarin-speaking talents and aspiring Chinese language educators. Students also had the opportunity to learn more about UPER's educational programs, organizational mission, and long-term vision of developing globally competitive Mandarin talents.

Together, the Career Forum and Job Fair reflected the shared commitment of UPER Education & Tech and Tarumanagara Xinya College to bridging academia and industry. Through career sharing, professional engagement, and direct interaction with students, the collaboration aimed to broaden students' career perspectives and better prepare them for future professional opportunities.
Bridging Education and Industry

Opening the forum, representatives from Tarumanagara Xinya College emphasized the growing importance of Mandarin proficiency in today's global economy. As international collaboration continues to expand, Mandarin has become more than just a language skill—it is now a strategic competency that enables graduates to connect with global opportunities and pursue careers across a wide range of industries.
Preparing Students for Global Career Opportunities

Throughout the forum, UPER Education & Tech shared insights into career development, international employment trends, and the evolving expectations of employers. Students learned that studying Mandarin or majoring in Mandarin Education no longer limits graduates to careers in teaching or translation. Instead, Mandarin proficiency, educational expertise, and cross-cultural communication skills have become valuable assets in fields such as human resources, business development, marketing, customer relationship management, international trade, cross-border e-commerce, education and training, and multinational corporations.

The forum also highlighted the changing qualities that companies seek in today's workforce. Beyond technical knowledge, employers increasingly value communication skills, professionalism, adaptability, problem-solving abilities, and a growth mindset. Participants received practical guidance on resume writing, interview preparation, workplace expectations, and long-term career planning, helping them better understand how to prepare for successful careers after graduation.

Another key topic was the role of HSK (Hanyu Shuiping Kaoshi) in supporting students' international development. Participants learned how HSK certification can serve as a pathway to scholarships at Chinese universities while also strengthening future career opportunities in Chinese companies, multinational corporations, and technology-driven industries.

The forum also featured an alumni sharing session, where students gained first-hand insights into the transition from university life to the professional world. Through real experiences, participants were encouraged to embrace continuous learning, develop strong communication skills, and actively seek opportunities for both personal and professional growth.
Building Indonesia's Mandarin Talent Ecosystem

As part of the event, UPER Education & Tech introduced its long-term vision of building a comprehensive Mandarin talent development ecosystem in Indonesia. Beyond language education, UPER is committed to connecting students with international study opportunities, professional training, industry exposure, and global career pathways. Through its integrated HSK → Study Pathway → China Industry Career Opportunity approach, UPER aims to support Indonesian students in developing the competencies needed to thrive in an increasingly interconnected world.

To date, UPER has established strategic partnerships with universities, schools, educational institutions, organizations, and companies across Indonesia and China. These collaborations continue to expand access to Mandarin education, HSK preparation, scholarship opportunities, professional development programs, and international career pathways for Indonesia's younger generation.

Further reinforcing its commitment to career development, UPER Education & Tech also participated as an official exhibitor at UNTAR Job Fair 2026, where students received consultations on Mandarin learning, study opportunities in China, scholarship pathways, and career opportunities in Chinese companies and international industries. The enthusiastic response from students reflected the growing recognition of Mandarin as a valuable competitive advantage in today's global workforce.

The successful co-hosting of the Tarumanagara Xinya College Career Forum 2026 marks another milestone in UPER Education & Tech's mission to bridge education, culture, and industry between Indonesia and China. Moving forward, UPER will continue strengthening collaborations with universities, educational institutions, and industry partners to create more opportunities for Indonesian youth through quality Mandarin education, international academic pathways, and meaningful career development.

As globalization continues to reshape the future of work, UPER Education & Tech remains committed to empowering the next generation with the language skills, global perspectives, and cross-cultural competencies needed to succeed in an increasingly connected world.

UPER Education & Tech attended the SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan Graduation Celebration as an education partner in a series of events, including the Mujonta Awards, Qur'an Graduation Ceremony, Outstanding Student Awards, and the launch of the Mujonta Integrated Learning and Excellence System (MILES), held at the UPN Veteran Yogyakarta Auditorium.

The event brought together prominent figures from the education sector, including Dr. Didik Suhardi, Ph.D., Special Staff to the Minister of Education; Dr. Muhammad Ikhwan Ahada, S.Ag., M.A., Chairman of the Regional Leadership of Muhammadiyah of the Special Region of Yogyakarta; Ahmad Muhamad, M.Ag., Chairman of the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council of the Regional Leadership of Muhammadiyah of the Special Region of Yogyakarta; Fika Widiana Kuspratiwi, M.Pd., Principal of SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan; and Eric Wang, Founder of UPER Education & Tech.

As an education partner, UPER Education & Tech sincerely appreciates the invitation from SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan and the trust placed in us to be part of this meaningful occasion. UPER are honored to work alongside the school in advancing this pilot project and benchmark school initiative for Chinese language education. The collaboration reflects a joint commitment to enriching students' educational experiences through Chinese language learning, international collaboration, and innovative educational initiatives.
Building a Pilot Model for Chinese Language Education in Yogyakarta
One of the event's highlights was the
Chinese Cultural Performance

, presented by students of SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan. The performance was the result of a dedicated Chinese language mentoring program conducted in advance by UPER Education & Tech's academic team and instructors. Through lessons focused on communication skills, pronunciation, and confidence building, the students confidently delivered their performance in Chinese before distinguished guests, demonstrating the encouraging outcomes of the school's newly introduced Chinese language program developed in collaboration with UPER Education & Tech.Although the journey toward future international education opportunities is still a long one, every meaningful achievement begins with a strong first step.
A Celebration of Achievement and Educational Innovation

This year's graduation celebration was not only a farewell to students completing their primary education but also a recognition of their academic and non-academic accomplishments. The program featured the Qur'an Graduation Ceremony, Outstanding Student Awards, the Mujonta Awards, and the launch of the Mujonta Integrated Learning and Excellence System (MILES), an educational framework designed to integrate academic excellence, character development, technological innovation, and spiritual values.Through these initiatives, SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan reaffirmed its commitment to developing students with strong character, leadership, academic excellence, and future-ready competencies.
An Inspiring Message for the Next Generation

During his remarks, Eric Wang congratulated the graduates, especially those completing the Qur'an Graduation Ceremony and receiving Outstanding.

Eric encouraged the graduates to view graduation not as the end of learning, but as the beginning of a lifelong journey of growth, exploration, and new opportunities.

"Never stop learning. Stay curious, ask questions, dare to try new things, and never be afraid of making mistakes. Every great achievement begins with a small step and the courage to keep moving forward,"
said Eric Wang.

He also emphasized the important role of schools and families in nurturing students' character, discipline, and passion for learning, highlighting that education is a shared responsibility in preparing future generations.
UPER's Commitment to Developing Globally Minded Future Leaders

As an education platform specializing in Chinese language education, international education consulting, teacher development, and educational partnerships, UPER Education & Tech is committed to expanding learning opportunities for Indonesian students. Through language education, cross-cultural exchange, and collaboration with schools, universities, and industry partners, the company aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to thrive in an increasingly interconnected world while contributing to the development of globally competitive, ethical, and future-ready human capital.
Advancing Education Towards Golden Indonesia 2045

UPER Education & Tech's participation in the SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan Graduation Celebration reflects the company's long-term commitment to strengthening collaboration with educational institutions across Indonesia through innovation, international collaboration, and the development of global competencies.

As the first pilot project and benchmark school for Chinese language education in Yogyakarta, SD Muhammadiyah Jogokariyan represents an important milestone in introducing Chinese language education at the elementary level while remaining firmly rooted in Qur'anic values and local identity. The initiative is expected to inspire more schools across Yogyakarta and beyond to embrace high-quality Chinese language education.

More importantly, this collaboration reflects a shared commitment among schools, families, and educational institutions to prepare Indonesia's younger generation for the future. By integrating Chinese language education with character development rooted in Qur'anic values, the initiative seeks to nurture students who are confident, open-minded, and globally competent while preserving their cultural identity. In doing so, it supports Indonesia's long-term vision of Golden Indonesia 2045 by contributing to the development of ethical, innovative, and future-ready human capital.

children.text: Jakarta, December 23, 2025

— The Workshop on Scholarship and Higher Education Opportunities in China, jointly organized by UPER Education, the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council (Dikdasmen & PNF) of the Central Executive Board of Muhammadiyah, and Central China Normal University (CCNU), was attended by approximately 160 participants, including school leaders, educators, parents, and students from various regions across Indonesia.
The workshop served as a strategic platform to expand access to international education information and to encourage Indonesian students’ preparedness for pursuing higher education in China.
The event was hosted by H. R. Alpha Amirrachman, M.Phil., Ph.D.,
Deputy Chairman of the Muhammadiyah Central Leadership Council for Elementary and Secondary Education
, with interpretation support provided by Fenny Laoshi,
HSK Teacher of UPER Education
, ensuring effective communication throughout the sessions for participants from both Indonesia and China.
Remarks from Muhammadiyah Leadership: Expanding Global Education Access
In a separate opening address, Didik Suhardi, Ph.D.,
Chairman of the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council (Dikdasmen & PNF) of the Central Executive Board of Muhammadiyah

, emphasized the importance of expanding global education access for Indonesia’s younger generation. He highlighted that opportunities to study abroad, particularly in China, are becoming increasingly accessible through various scholarship schemes.

He further stressed that strong character development, academic readiness, and structured guidance are key factors enabling Indonesian students to adapt and succeed in international academic environments. Schools were encouraged to actively leverage global education partnerships to enhance the quality of Indonesia’s human resources.
CCNU Presentation: A Leading University in Central China

At the same time, the session was delivered by Prof. Zhang Yichuan, Deputy Director of the Department of International Cooperation, Central China Normal University (CCNU). In his presentation, Prof. Zhang introduced CCNU as a leading comprehensive university under China’s Ministry of Education, with a long-standing history dating back to 1903.

He explained that CCNU offers a complete education system from undergraduate to doctoral and postdoctoral levels, with 12 disciplines ranked in the top 1% worldwide according to the ESI global rankings. Prof. Zhang also shared updates on the development of CCNU’s new Panlongcheng Campus, which is scheduled to welcome its first cohort of students in 2028 and is strategically located near Wuhan International Airport. In addition, he expressed CCNU’s strong interest in further deepening cooperation with partners in Indonesia through expanded academic exchanges, joint programs, and broader student mobility initiatives.
UPER Education: Bridging Indonesian Students to Global Education
Following the CCNU presentation,
Eric Wang, MBA
Founder of UPER Education

, shared strategic insights on the importance of international education as a long-term investment for Indonesian youth. He emphasized that proficiency in Mandarin and study experience in China not only enhance academic competence but also open broader career opportunities and global professional networks.

Eric Wang reaffirmed UPER Education’s commitment to serving as a bridge between Indonesia and China by providing integrated support services, including Mandarin language training, academic major consultation, and comprehensive guidance throughout the university and scholarship application process.
Admission Pathways and Scholarship Opportunities at CCNU

In addition, the workshop invited Li Minlin Laoshi and Zhao Shengmen Laoshi, Senior Admission Officers of Central China Normal University, to introduce detailed information on academic programs and admission opportunities at CCNU.

Li Minlin Laoshi focused on presenting CCNU’s academic offerings, including degree programs taught in both Mandarin and English, as well as a range of short-term programs designed for international students. She highlighted the diversity of disciplines available at CCNU and the flexibility of study pathways that cater to different academic backgrounds and learning objectives.

Meanwhile, Zhao Shengmen Laoshi provided a comprehensive explanation of the application procedures and scholarship opportunities at CCNU. She outlined various scholarship schemes offered by the Chinese government and the university, covering tuition fees, accommodation, medical insurance, and monthly living allowances, which enable international students—particularly those from Indonesia—to pursue higher education in China with strong institutional support.

These scholarships include tuition waivers, accommodation, medical insurance, and monthly living allowances, offering Indonesian students the opportunity to pursue high-quality education in China with affordable financial support.
UPER Education’s Student Support and School Partnership Programs

In a subsequent session, Zainul Fitri, Project Manager of UPER Education, presented UPER Education’s structured support programs, including HSK training, university workshops, campus visit programs, and intensive mentoring for schools and students planning to continue their studies in China.
These programs are designed to systematically prepare students’ language skills, academic readiness, and study planning starting from the secondary education level.
Sharing Session: Indonesian Student Experience at CCNU

The workshop also featured a sharing session by Mesa, an Indonesian student currently studying at Central China Normal University. She shared her firsthand experience of campus life, the inclusive learning environment, comprehensive facilities, and academic support available to international students in Wuhan.
Her testimony provided participants with a realistic perspective on studying and living in China as an international student.
Sustained Commitment to Indonesia–China Educational Collaboration

Through this workshop, UPER Education, Central China Normal University, and the Dikdasmen & PNF Council of the Muhammadiyah Central Executive Board reaffirmed their joint commitment to expanding Indonesia–China educational collaboration. Future initiatives include short-term study programs, student and faculty exchanges, teacher training, and joint education pathways.
This workshop is expected to serve as a concrete step toward opening wider global education opportunities for Indonesian students.

children.text: 16 December 2025 — UPER Education Technology successfully organized the
China–Indonesia Education Advancement Student Forum

, conducted in a hybrid format (online and offline). The forum engaged over 100 Indonesian high school and university students representing 9 partner high schools, alongside official representatives from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (ZSTU) and key Indonesian education partners, including Muhammadiyah Organization.
The event served as a strategic platform to strengthen structured and sustainable international education pathways between Indonesia and China.

The forum was specifically designed to provide early-stage international education exposure for Indonesian students, with a strong focus on China as a higher education destination. The event was attended by over 160 participants, including more than 120 senior high school students (Grades 10–12), as well as representatives of teachers and school principals from eight schools, who received systematic guidance on academic preparation, Mandarin language readiness, CSCA pathways, and scholarship opportunities—equipping them with clear and actionable steps toward global higher education.
UPER Education Technology: A Five-Pillar Education Bridge between Indonesia and China

As the organizer, Eric Wang, Founder of UPER Education Technology, emphasized that China has five major educational regions—North China, East China, Central China, South China, and Southwest China—covering more than ten popular cities and hundreds of high-quality universities, offering diverse and flexible study options for international students. UPER is committed to serving as a strategic bridge between Indonesian high schools and Chinese universities, building a clear and systematic pathway for students’ academic advancement.

Through in-depth partnerships with Chinese universities such as Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, UPER supports Indonesian students in achieving a smooth transition from high school to international higher education. In his remarks, Wang reaffirmed the importance of early planning and pledged that UPER would provide one-stop, end-to-end support starting from the high school stage, including Mandarin language training, academic planning, and university and scholarship applications—empowering students to seize opportunities to study in China while advancing educational cooperation and people-to-people exchange between China and Indonesia.
Character Education and Global Perspective: Remarks by Muhammadiyah Leadership

Representing Indonesia’s education community, H. R. Alpha Amirrachman, M.Phil., Ph.D., Deputy Chairman of the Muhammadiyah Central Leadership Council for Elementary and Secondary Education, delivered a keynote reflection emphasizing the importance of balancing academic achievement with strong character development.

He stressed that international education should not only prepare students to compete globally but also strengthen integrity, discipline, and social responsibility, encouraging students to become future leaders who contribute positively to society and the nation.

Representing Indonesia’s education community, H. R. Alpha Amirrachman, M.Phil., Ph.D., Deputy Chairman of the Muhammadiyah Central Leadership Council for Elementary and Secondary Education, international education should strike a balance between academic excellence and character development, cultivating future leaders who possess both global competitiveness and a strong sense of social responsibility.

Guided by this vision, China—one of the world’s key engines of development—offers a unique platform for Indonesian youth. Studying in China and gaining a deep understanding of its language, culture, and development model can help nurture leaders with strong integrity and practical capabilities, while fostering sustained cooperation between China and Indonesia across multiple sectors and achieving shared growth and mutual benefit.
Direct Insights from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University

The forum also featured Mr. Ray Shi, Director of the International Student Admissions Office at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, who delivered a focused presentation addressing key concerns of Indonesian high school graduates, including admission requirements, scholarship policies, and student support systems.
Following this, Ms. Sienna Jiang, Senior Admissions Officer from the International Education College, provided a comprehensive overview of academic programs, campus life, and application timelines, giving students a clear understanding of study opportunities in China.

During the forum, Mr. Shi highlighted that Hangzhou, known as both a “Paradise on Earth” and a global hub of digital innovation, offers international students a unique environment that blends natural beauty with modern industry. Leveraging its century-long academic heritage and strong disciplines such as textiles and mechanical engineering, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University offers dual-track programs in English and Chinese, an extensive global partnership network, and a well-established scholarship system aimed at cultivating internationally competitive professionals.

He emphasized the university’s strong commitment to educational exchange with Indonesia, expressing its willingness to provide high-quality platforms for Indonesian students to pursue both academic and career development in Hangzhou—empowering them to become bridges for future cooperation between China and Indonesia.

Subsequently, Ms. Jiang, Senior Admissions Officer from the International Education College, delivered an in-depth explanation of degree programs, scholarship opportunities, and application procedures. Outstanding Indonesian student representatives, Ye and Wu, also shared their experiences in language learning, campus life, and cultural exchange, showcasing Zhejiang Sci-Tech University’s diverse and inclusive international learning environment.
Real Student Experiences: Campus Life and Living Environment at ZSTU

Denise Yahya Miharja and Kallista Ulansky, Indonesian students studying Chinese language at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, shared practical insights into campus life and the living environment. They introduced key facilities, including the library, sports centers, stadium, swimming pool, and green spaces, highlighting the completeness and accessibility of campus infrastructure.

They also explained daily living aspects such as international student dormitories, transportation access, affordable dining options across multiple campus canteens, the availability of halal food nearby, and various activities for international students, including cultural events, competitions, internship support, and job fairs.

Lauren, an Indonesian student at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (ZSTU), shared her experience after living and studying in Hangzhou for over two and a half years. She described the city and campus environment as very safe, especially for female students, supported by extensive security presence and CCTV across campus, dormitories, and surrounding areas. She also highlighted Hangzhou’s clean, well-organized urban environment, its natural beauty during autumn, famous landmarks such as West Lake, and the convenience of daily life, including cashless payments via Alipay and WeChat Pay, free delivery for online shopping, and efficient transportation options like public bicycles, e-bikes, campus shuttle buses, and high-speed trains.

She further explained that ZSTU offers complete campus facilities, including indoor and outdoor sports courts, football fields, running tracks, and student-friendly infrastructure. For international students, the university regularly organizes cultural events, talent competitions, group trips, and social activities, such as visits to Yiwu, Songcheng cultural park, Chinese New Year celebrations, tea ceremonies, and traditional festivals. These activities not only enrich student life but also provide opportunities to build international friendships and cross-cultural connections, making campus life active, inclusive, and well-supported.
Student Representative Engagement from Partner High Schools

The activity was designed as a focused recruitment and collaboration initiative involving eight nearby partner high schools, where each school selected student representatives to directly express their academic interests, intended majors, and expectations for higher education. This approach enabled students to articulate their study aspirations firsthand, while allowing university admission officers to understand student demand more precisely and efficiently.

Through direct dialogue, students raised concrete questions regarding academic programs, teaching methods, campus facilities, scholarship opportunities, living environment, and future career pathways. This one-stop communication model significantly improved enrollment efficiency by connecting student intentions, school partners, and university admissions officers within a single, structured platform.
Focus on HSK and CSCA as Core Admission Pathways

During the forum, Zainul Fikri, Representative of UPER Education Indonesia, emphasized that HSK and CSCA are the two key academic qualifications required for Indonesian students to access undergraduate study and scholarship opportunities at Chinese universities, including Zhejiang Sci-Tech University.

He explained that UPER’s continuous program is structured from Grade 10 to Grade 12, beginning with HSK preparation as the foundation of Mandarin proficiency, followed by advanced HSK levels and academic readiness, and culminating in CSCA preparation, which has been officially implemented in 2025 as a mandatory entrance assessment for undergraduate applicants.

UPER provides specialized HSK courses (Levels 1–4 and above) and CSCA preparation programs, taught by experienced Chinese and Indonesian instructors, to ensure students meet admission requirements efficiently. Through this one-stop pathway, UPER aligns language training, examination preparation, and university admission into a single, streamlined system to improve enrollment efficiency for both students and university admissions officers.
Shaping the Future of China–Indonesia Educational Cooperation

The forum concluded with a shared commitment among UPER Education Technology, partner universities, and participating schools to continue expanding student-focused initiatives, strengthen academic collaboration, and develop sustainable education pathways for Indonesian high school students.

UPER Education Technology remains committed to empowering Indonesian youth with global opportunities and looks forward to organizing more international education forums and preparation programs in the future.

In the final session of the forum, UPER Education Technology, together with its partner universities and participating schools, jointly reaffirmed their commitment to advancing student-centered collaborative programs, deepening academic cooperation between China and Indonesia, and building sustainable and diversified pathways for Indonesian high school students to pursue higher education. As one of UPER’s key strategic partner institutions, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University exemplified UPER’s professional capability in connecting Indonesian students with high-quality higher education resources in China.

Looking ahead, UPER will continue to anchor its efforts across five core educational regions—North China, Central China, South China, Southwest China, and East China—covering more than ten popular study-abroad cities and over one hundred partner universities. Through a series of ongoing recruitment briefings and educational exchange initiatives, UPER aims to further strengthen educational alignment between China and Indonesia, empowering more Indonesian students to access global education opportunities and achieve mutual talent development and shared growth.

children.text: South Tangerang, 4 December 2025

— UPER Education Technology, in partnership with Zhejiang Sci-Tech University (ZSTU) and with full support from the Forum of Private School Principals of South Tangerang (FKKSS), successfully hosted the China–Indonesia Education Advancement Forum. The event brought together principals and academic leaders from top Indonesian high schools, including Muhammadiyah 8 High School and Thursina International Islamic Boarding School.

Held in a hybrid format, the forum carried the theme “Strengthening Educational Cooperation and Cultivating Future Talent Together,” marking a significant step forward in expanding bilateral academic collaboration and broadening international study opportunities for Indonesian students.
UPER, FKKSS, and ZSTU Set the Direction for Future Collaboration

The forum opened with remarks from Dr. Vivian Chen, Dean of the International Education College at ZSTU. She highlighted the steady increase in Indonesian students pursuing higher education in China and emphasized that educational cooperation serves as a strong bridge between the two nations. Dr. Chen also introduced Hangzhou’s unique position as both a cultural landmark and a hub for digital innovation, while presenting ZSTU’s academic strengths and international development roadmap.

Following this, Ray Shi, Director of the Admission Office (International Student Office) at ZSTU, presented the university’s admission policies, scholarship programs, international curriculum pathways, and updates on Indonesian students currently studying at ZSTU. His presentation provided clear guidance on how Indonesian students can prepare and transition into Chinese higher education.

its academic strengths and international programs,

curriculum alignment,
strengthening Mandarin programs,
student and teacher exchange opportunities,
and preparation for overseas study pathways.

academic counseling,
university application guidance,
major recommendations based on student interest,
scholarship consultation,
and complete administrative support.
Constructive Dialogue Facilitated by UPER, ZSTU, and FKKSS
A dynamic Q&A session addressed practical concerns raised by school leaders, including:
university admission requirements and scholarship pathways in China,
Mandarin proficiency expectations (HSK),
campus life and cultural adaptation,
availability of campus tour programs,

UPER, ZSTU, and FKKSS offered comprehensive answers, demonstrating a shared commitment to supporting Indonesian students through transparent and well-structured processes.

The MoU establishes a long-term cooperation framework that includes:
developing a study-in-China information and preparation center,
academic training and counseling programs for students,
strengthened scholarship pathways and university recommendations,
joint activities such as seminars, workshops, and campus tours.
FKKSS welcomed the MoU signing as an important step in strengthening the internationalization agenda of private schools across South Tangerang.
A New Milestone for China–Indonesia Educational Cooperation
The forum concluded with a shared commitment from UPER, ZSTU, and FKKSS—together with participating schools—to:
develop joint talent-development programs,
expand student exchange and short-course opportunities,
build a cross-border school partnership network,
and strengthen long-term pathways for Indonesian students pursuing higher education in China.
UPER Education Technology is committed to expanding this collaboration model to additional FKKSS member schools and deepening China–Indonesia educational cooperation in the years ahead.

UPER Education Technology officially established a Mandarin Language Center in Yogyakarta as part of a strategic collaboration with the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council (Dikdasmen PNF) of the Central Board of Muhammadiyah. This initiative represents a significant step toward strengthening Mandarin language education, expanding access to international academic pathways, and fostering global talent development within the Muhammadiyah education network.

The collaboration was formally highlighted during the National Coordination Meeting (Rakornas) of the Dikdasmen PNF Council. During the forum, Uper's strategic direction toward global education partnerships, scholarship access, and international academic networking was emphasized.

At the meeting, Ms. Suki Zhou, Vice President of UPER Education Technology, attended alongside Mr. Didik Suhardi, Chairman of the Dikdasmen PNF Council of the Central Board of Muhammadiyah, Mr. R. Alpha Amirrachman, MPhil, PhD, Vice Chairman of the Dikdasmen & PNF Council, and Mr. Agus Suroyo, M.Pd.I, Director of Matahari Global Edu. Together, they participated in the official presentation session and conducted a plaque presentation ceremony marking the launch of the Mandarin Language Center initiative.

Prior to this national-level highlight, the formal signing ceremony was previously conducted in Yogyakarta and attended by Mr. Eric Wang, Founder of UPER Education Technology, who was present to witness and support the signing of the cooperation agreement, reaffirming UPER’s long-term commitment to educational collaboration in Indonesia.
Mandarin Language Center and HSK-Based Academic Programs

The Mandarin Language Center initiated by UPER Education Technology provides structured Mandarin instruction aligned with international HSK (Hanyu Shuiping Kaoshi) standards. The program is designed to systematically develop students’ language proficiency from foundational to advanced levels, ensuring measurable academic progress.

The learning model integrates experienced local instructors with native Mandarin-speaking educators in a hybrid structure, supported by academic collaboration in curriculum development and language standards.

In addition to the offline classes conducted in Yogyakarta, UPER will invite distinguished academic experts and senior professors from leading language universities in China to deliver online lectures.

The online format is adopted to provide students with direct access to top-tier language specialists and renowned professors based in China, ensuring high-quality instruction and authentic academic engagement.
Strengthening Global Academic and Career Pathways

Through its academic and institutional network, UPER Education Technology supports students in gaining structured preparation for higher education opportunities in China. The program strengthens students’ readiness for international academic mobility, scholarship access, and cross-cultural engagement.

Beyond language proficiency, this initiative reflects a broader strategic framework focused on developing globally competent talent equipped to engage within the Indonesia–China academic and industrial ecosystem.
Institutional Commitment to Educational Internationalization

The establishment of the Mandarin Language Center in Yogyakarta demonstrates UPER Education Technology’s strategic commitment to long-term educational internationalization. By combining standardized HSK-based language training with international academic connectivity, UPER aims to empower future generations with competitive global competencies.

This collaboration is expected to serve as a replicable model for structured Mandarin education development across regions, reinforcing institutional cooperation between Indonesian and Chinese educational stakeholders.

children.text: UPER Education Technology officially established a collaboration with the Council for Elementary and Secondary Education and Non-Formal Education (Dikdasmen & PNF) of the Central Board of Muhammadiyah on 8 January 2026. The event was held at the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education Office (Kemendikdasmen), Building A, 2nd Floor, Jakarta, starting at 13.00 WIB.

This collaboration represents a strategic step in strengthening internationally oriented education, particularly in developing structured education pathways between Indonesia and the People’s Republic of China. It aligns with Muhammadiyah’s growing emphasis in recent years on organizational internationalization, including within the education sector.

The Dikdasmen & PNF Council of Muhammadiyah plays a key role in managing and overseeing thousands of Muhammadiyah schools, madrasahs, and Islamic boarding schools across Indonesia, while coordinating closely with education authorities at provincial and local levels. Through this collaboration, Muhammadiyah and UPER Education Technology share a commitment to expanding access to well-structured and sustainable international education opportunities for students and educators.

From Muhammadiyah’s perspective, this collaboration is aimed at strengthening study abroad orientation within Muhammadiyah schools and higher education institutions, ensuring that students are better prepared academically, linguistically, and globally to pursue international education pathways. From UPER Education Technology’s perspective, as an education consultancy specializing in China-focused education pathways, this collaboration reflects UPER’s role as a strategic partner in providing comprehensive and globally aligned international education support.

The collaboration covers a range of joint educational initiatives focused on enhancing global competencies. One of the initial areas of focus is Mandarin language training, designed as a foundational component for the development of broader international education pathways. The programs are intended for junior high school students, senior high and vocational school students, university students, as well as teachers and lecturers, with initial implementation in selected schools before gradual expansion across the Muhammadiyah education network nationwide.

Through this collaboration, students are expected to gain structured access to Mandarin language learning and Chinese cultural studies, improved academic and linguistic readiness for higher education at leading universities in China, and opportunities to obtain internationally recognized certifications such as HSK and the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA). The collaboration also opens opportunities for participation in short-term study programs and academic visits to China, as well as pathways for international career development, particularly for vocational students.

For Muhammadiyah schools and madrasahs, this collaboration is expected to strengthen flagship programs through the integration of Mandarin and international education, enhance the capacity of teachers and school leaders through training and professional development, reinforce institutional reputation as globally oriented schools, and support the development of international program management and academic infrastructure.

In the medium and long term, the collaboration is expected to generate strategic impact across the Muhammadiyah education ecosystem, including the development of regional centers of excellence for Mandarin language and Chinese studies, the establishment of sustainable international education pathways from secondary to higher education, enhanced global competitiveness of Muhammadiyah graduates, and the initial foundation for an international study and career planning center for students and alumni.

Mr. Didik Suhardi, PhD, Chairman of the Dikdasmen & PNF Council of the Central Board of Muhammadiyah, stated that this collaboration reflects Muhammadiyah’s commitment to expanding access to international education while strengthening global literacy and foreign language proficiency as part of its broader educational transformation. He emphasized that the initiative is a strategic step in preparing globally competitive generations who remain firmly rooted in Islamic and national values.

Meanwhile, Ms. Zhou Suting (Suki), Vice President of UPER Education Technology, highlighted UPER’s role as a bridge between Indonesian and Chinese education systems. She reaffirmed UPER’s commitment to delivering practical Mandarin education and structured, sustainable international education pathways that support Muhammadiyah’s vision of building an internationally competitive education ecosystem.

This collaboration is expected to serve as a strong foundation for long-term partnership between UPER Education Technology and Muhammadiyah in advancing inclusive, globally connected, and future-oriented education.

children.text: On April 9, 2026, UPER Education Technology held a strategic meeting with the Faculty of Economics and Business (FEB), Universitas Negeri Jakarta (UNJ) to explore potential collaboration in advancing international education. The meeting marked the first step toward establishing a strategic partnership focused on Mandarin language training, HSK certification, academic mobility, as well as internship and student exchange opportunities in China.

The meeting brought together key representatives from Faculty of Economics and Business UNJ, including Darma Rika Swaramarinda, S.Pd., M.S.E., Ph.D., Vice Dean for Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, and Alumni; Andi Muhammad Sadat, S.E., M.Si., Coordinator of the Applied Bachelor's Program in Digital Marketing; Putri Haryani, S.Tr.Ak., M.Sc., Head of the Internationalization Laboratory; and Nofriska Krissanya, S.E., M.B.A., Head of the Quality Assurance Unit.

Representing UPER Education were Ms. Suki, Co-Founder; Mr Zainul, Senior Business Development Manager; Ms Fenny, Academic Director ; and Ms Dewi, Finance Manager. The meeting provided an important platform for both institutions to align their vision of equipping students with the global competencies required in today's increasingly interconnected academic and professional landscape。
Addressing the Growing Demand for International Academic Opportunities

During the discussion, FEB UNJ highlighted the increasing interest among both undergraduate and postgraduate students in pursuing double degree programs, student exchange opportunities, and internships in China. However, one of the key challenges identified is the language proficiency requirement, as many international programs require applicants to obtain HSK Level 3 or Level 4 certification before participation.

Recognizing this growing demand, UPER Education presented its comprehensive Mandarin education ecosystem designed to prepare students with the language proficiency and international competencies needed to pursue academic and career opportunities in China.
UPER Education's Comprehensive Approach to Global Competency Development

UPER Education introduced its Mandarin language training system, which integrates internationally recognized curricula, experienced educators, and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered learning technology. The program is developed based on the academic framework of Beijing Language and Culture University (BLCU) and is delivered by highly qualified instructors, including native Mandarin-speaking teachers.

In addition to language education, UPER Education showcased its extensive academic network with leading Chinese universities, including Beijing Language and Culture University (BLCU), University of International Business and Economics (UIBE), and China Central Normal University (CCNU). Through these partnerships, students may gain access to academic exchange programs, collaborative research opportunities, scholarship pathways, and internships with partner organizations and leading Chinese enterprises.
Proposed Areas of Cooperation
As part of the preliminary discussions, both institutions explored several areas of cooperation that will serve as the foundation for a future Faculty-level Memorandum of Agreement (MoA).

The proposed collaboration covers a wide range of initiatives aimed at strengthening students' international competencies and expanding academic cooperation between both institutions. Key areas include:

Mandarin Language Education and HSK Preparation, providing structured Mandarin language training and HSK preparation programs to equip students with the language proficiency required for international academic and career opportunities.

Student Referral and Career Opportunities, enabling qualified students with Mandarin proficiency to access internship and employment opportunities with Chinese-funded enterprises and international companies.
Language Center Programs, including Mandarin courses for students at different academic levels, graduation HSK preparation programs, and customized training based on students' language proficiency.
Academic Exchange, through seminars, workshops, curriculum development, and other collaborative academic activities that strengthen educational cooperation between Indonesia and China.

On-Campus Program Implementation, allowing UPER Education to organize Mandarin training programs and educational activities directly within the Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Negeri Jakarta.

Regional Development and Brand Cooperation, leveraging UPER Education's network to expand Mandarin education initiatives while strengthening the university's international engagement and promoting high-quality Chinese language education.

Through these proposed areas of cooperation, both institutions aim to establish a sustainable partnership that supports students' academic development, enhances employability, and promotes international collaboration.
Launching a Pilot Project

As an initial step in the collaboration, both parties discussed launching a pilot program consisting of career development workshops and Mandarin language skills training for students from the Faculty of Economics and Business, Universitas Negeri Jakarta (FEB UNJ).

The initiative is intended to lay the foundation for broader academic and international collaboration between the two institutions, while helping students better prepare for China-focused academic and career opportunities, including international exchange programs, overseas internships, further studies in China, and employment with Chinese-funded enterprises.
Commitment to Long-Term Academic Collaboration

The meeting concluded with a shared commitment to continue developing the proposed partnership through the preparation of a Faculty-level Memorandum of Agreement (MoA). The partnership team from FEB UNJ and the Business Development team from UPER Education will work collaboratively to finalize the draft agreement and schedule subsequent technical meetings to discuss the implementation of the pilot project and future collaborative initiatives.

children.text: Yogyakarta, June 5, 2026 — UPER Education & Technology participated in and supported the official launch of the Mandarin Learning Center at SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Yogyakarta (SMA Moega). The inauguration marks an important milestone in the development of Mandarin education within the Muhammadiyah educational ecosystem and reflects a shared commitment to expanding international education opportunities for Indonesian students.

Supported by UPER Education & Technology and its educational partners, the Mandarin Learning Center is expected to become a strategic platform for language learning, cross-cultural understanding, international academic mobility, and future career development.
The event, held at KH Ahmad Dahlan Hall, SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Yogyakarta, brought together educational leaders, Muhammadiyah representatives, school principals, and international education partners.

The event was attended by senior representatives from the government, Muhammadiyah educational institutions, schools, and international education organizations. Distinguished attendees included Dr. Iwan Junaedi, S.Si., M.Pd., Director of Principals, School Supervisors, and Educational Personnel; Didik Suhardi, Ph.D., Chairman of the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council (Dikdasmen & PNF) of Muhammadiyah’s Central Executive Board; Muhammad Khoirul Huda, M.Pd., Secretary General of Dikdasmen Muhammadiyah; Reni Herawati, representative of Dikdasmen & PNF PWM DIY; Sutomo, M.Ag., Chairman of the Muhammadiyah Teachers Forum; Agus Suroyo, M.Pd., Director of Matahari Global Education (MGE); Fitri Sari Sukmawati, M.Pd., Principal of SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Yogyakarta; as well as representatives from UPER Education & Technology.
Growing Recognition of the Importance of Mandarin Education

The establishment of the Mandarin Learning Center reflects the growing recognition of Mandarin as an essential skill for future generations. As cooperation between Indonesia and China continues to expand across education, business, technology, and industry, Mandarin proficiency is becoming an increasingly valuable asset for students seeking international opportunities.
In her opening remarks, Fitri Sari Sukmawati, M.Pd., Principal of SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Yogyakarta, shared that the school has been implementing Mandarin classes over the past year as part of its internationalization strategy.

“We have implemented Mandarin classes over the past year as part of our educational development. Moving forward, bilingual education will continue to be one of our flagship programs as we work toward becoming a globally oriented school,” she stated.
She also emphasized that becoming a Mandarin Learning Center carries significant responsibility and represents an opportunity to contribute more broadly to Muhammadiyah and Indonesian society.
UPER: Mandarin as a Gateway to International Opportunities

Representing UPER Education & Technology, Mr. Eric, Founder of UPER, expressed his appreciation for the establishment of the Mandarin Learning Center and emphasized the importance of building educational bridges between Indonesia and China.
In his keynote speech, Mr. Eric explained that learning Mandarin should not be viewed merely as acquiring a language skill, but as gaining access to global education resources, cultural understanding, and international career opportunities.

According to Mr. Eric, UPER has established partnerships with more than 100 higher education institutions across China, including comprehensive universities, engineering institutions, teacher-training universities, and vocational colleges.
Through these partnerships, Indonesian students can access scholarship opportunities, academic progression pathways, student exchange programs, and international career development opportunities.

“Language is only the starting point. What truly matters is that through language, students gain access to broader educational resources, different cultural perspectives, and more opportunities to shape their future,” said Mr. Eric.
He further highlighted that as Chinese enterprises continue expanding internationally, demand for professionals with Mandarin proficiency and global perspectives is also increasing rapidly.
National Education Leaders Highlight the Importance of Mandarin Learning

One of the most anticipated moments of the event was the keynote address delivered by Didik Suhardi, Ph.D., Chairman of the Primary, Secondary, and Non-Formal Education Council (Dikdasmen & PNF) of the Central Executive Board of Muhammadiyah.

In his remarks, Didik Suhardi emphasized that foreign language proficiency has become one of the essential competencies that future generations must develop in order to navigate the demands of a rapidly changing global landscape.

He highlighted the growing cooperation between Indonesia and China across various sectors, including education, industry, technology, and business, creating increasing demand for individuals who possess both international perspectives and strong language skills.

“Language is one of the key competencies that future generations must possess. There are many opportunities arising from Indonesia–China cooperation that can be utilized by our young people. At the same time, many companies in Indonesia are looking for talents with international insight and foreign language capabilities,” he stated.

According to Didik Suhardi, educational institutions play a crucial role in preparing students not only with academic knowledge but also with global competencies that will enable them to compete and contribute in an increasingly interconnected world.

His remarks reinforced the significance of establishing the Mandarin Learning Center as a strategic initiative that supports the development of globally minded students and strengthens Indonesia’s future human capital.
Official Unveiling of the Mandarin Learning Center and Partnership Plaque

The launch also attracted significant attention from regional and national media outlets, reflecting growing public interest in international education and Mandarin learning initiatives. The event was subsequently covered by multiple Indonesian media organizations, highlighting its importance within both educational and community development sectors.

The event concluded with the official unveiling of the Mandarin Learning Center plaque and partnership logo, symbolizing the beginning of a long-term collaboration between Muhammadiyah, SMA Muhammadiyah 3 Yogyakarta, Matahari Global Education (MGE), and UPER Education & Technology.
The launch represents a shared commitment to building an educational ecosystem that connects Indonesian students with international opportunities and future-ready competencies.
Building Globally Competitive Indonesian Talent

Through this initiative, the Mandarin Learning Center is expected to serve not only as a language learning hub but also as a gateway to international education, scholarships, cultural exchange programs, and global career opportunities.

As an international education partner, UPER Education & Technology remains committed to providing educational resources, university networks, scholarship pathways, and industry connections that empower Indonesian students to achieve their full potential on the global stage.

As Indonesia continues to strengthen its engagement with the global community, initiatives such as the Mandarin Learning Center demonstrate the value of collaboration between schools, educational organizations, and international partners in preparing future generations with the language skills, global mindset, and international competencies required to thrive in an interconnected world.
